sample.marker: DBX MCP 0.4.127: benign enum dispatch; bind RWX calls to allocator

provenance.sources: forager fetched exact npm package, registry version records, and GitHub codeload archives by the registry gitHead commits; originals and .forage.json sidecars retained in scratch/version-drift
provenance.limits: The gitHead is a registry claim; no reproducible source-to-binary build or deployed configuration is available.

decisive_diff: Both packages contain package.json, README.md, and bin/dbx-mcp.exe. Manifests differ only in version, with no install hooks.
Binary size increases from 34,503,680 to 34,570,240 bytes. Import symbol sets are identical.

Each binary has 802 original CMOV/MOVSXD/ADD/indirect-jump matches, all using indexed enum tables. The current rules reproduce the suspicious match on 0.4.126 too, refuting newly introduced obfuscation.

Source changes add local documentation notes to schema tool responses, escaped as untrusted data, plus SQL Server endpoint parsing, MySQL checkout timeouts, PostgreSQL text-result fallback, Redis cursor isolation and other database fixes. Cargo.lock changes local package versions and removes the PostgreSQL test portpicker dependency.
New binary strings /api/docs/annotations/load, Local schema notes in this result, and the PostgreSQL binary-result fallback diagnostic agree with those source changes; all are absent from 0.4.126.
reverse_engineering: PE entry 0x141ac5120 initializes the CRT security cookie then transfers to normal CRT startup. TLS callback 0x1418e9554 handles DLL_THREAD_DETACH, obtains TLS values and locks cleanup state.

At VA 0x14000c549, read a Rust enum discriminant; BTC clears its niche/sign bit, CMOVS selects a tag, indexed MOVSXD reads a relative jump table. Arms emit null, boolean literals and object braces through writer routines. Additional matches dispatch future/state variants via indexed tables, not pointer-selected flattened branches.

Source startup opens local DBX storage or an explicitly configured DBX_WEB_URL backend, then serves MCP via stdio or the configured HTTP transport. HTTP validates bearer token, host and origin; query tools apply per-connection SQL policy. Database connections, keyring credentials, SSH/tunnels, driver process execution, crypto and filesystem operations accord with this role.

All six reported RWX spans lead across a direct call or branch to GetProcessHeap. Five paths use element-layout deallocation helper 0x1400c35a5, another uses 0x140e5a9e9; both multiply element count by r9 element size and eventually tail-call 0x140d8bb3f / HeapFree. The literal 64 is not page protection.

Decoded string facts include incidental Base64/hex hits and six VTTTTTTT XOR-stack values, not decoded executable stages. No concealed payload, persistence or unauthorized data-transfer chain was established.

rule_changes.correction: Require unindexed register-indirect MOVSXD (ModRM mod=00, excluding SIB and RIP-relative encodings), retaining the 12-site threshold; name the pointer-selected relative jumps. Real positives retain 682/696 and 101/103 qualifying sites respectively in independent Capstone decoding.

Preserve the original broad sequence matcher and 12-site threshold as a notable static code property. Operands were never bound across instructions, so this observation alone claims neither concealment nor proven data flow.

Resolve RIP-relative indirect calls to the VirtualAlloc IAT slot and reject intervening E8 bytes conservatively. Retain full null-address, variable-size, reserve/commit, RWX register-call setup. Description now explicitly identifies a call setup.

consumer_audit.dispatch: No exact YAML consumers; three ancestor obfuscation consumers are JavaScript-scoped and cannot consume these PE observations. Original fixture inventory and two real positive binaries inspected.
consumer_audit.allocation: Reviewed pe-embedded-blob-rwx-copy-and-run and unsigned-defender-export-rwx-loader-list consumers. The full register-call alternative is retained; the latter hostile composite remains present on rebrrgb.dll.
consumer_audit.limits: Opcode checks in the import alternative are conservative byte checks, not general x64 data-flow recovery.

losses: Only the unsupported suspicious obfuscation claim and notable RWX claim disappear on this package; the broad conditional-branch sequence remains notable. Other existing findings are retained.
classifier_disagreement: No disagreement on DBX. Positive control rebrrgb.dll retains one hostile and three suspicious findings, yet its ML level changes 15000 to -1 (probability 0.99890697 to 0.99587065). This is an exposed classifier regression, not justification for restoring inaccurate traits. thrgf.exe remains ML-benign at level -1 despite its retained suspicious dispatch finding, a pre-existing miss.
